zh.title: 達美航空波音737-900ER只飛北美內陸 為何仍保留ETOPS延程認證
zh.summary: 達美航空的波音737-900ER只飛北美內陸航線，卻仍有約20架維持ETOPS-180認證；這並非為了飛越洋航線，而是為了加勒比海航線更有效率的航路，以及夏威夷航線的備降需求——只是認證成本高昂，達美已把多數飛機的延程設備拆除，聯合航空則反其道而行，全數737都維持認證。
body: 達美航空2011年訂購100架波音737-900ER，2015年加訂20架、2017年再加訂10架，總數130架，疫情後又購入33架二手飛機，2013年起陸續交機。這款737家族最大衍生型已成為達美北美內陸航線的主力，但它並不以長航程見長，也從未飛越洋航線；儘管如此，達美仍讓部分737-900ER維持ETOPS-180認證，也就是可在距離備降機場180分鐘航程內飛行。

ETOPS是「延程雙發動機運作性能標準」，認證代表雙發動機客機能在距離備降機場60分鐘航程以上飛行，數字即為與機場的距離分鐘數。取得認證並不便宜：飛機須加裝額外通訊與導航設備、依專屬延程維護計畫保養，每次飛行前須由具延程資格的維修人員完成檢查，發動機還須由兩名不同技師分別檢查。達美如今只保留約20架具認證的737-900ER，其餘多數已拆除額外設備、不再按延程標準維護；相較之下，聯合航空737機隊全數640架與61架757都具認證，連主要飛休士頓出發短程國內線的12架737-900也不例外。

達美最初為737-900ER規畫了更大的角色。2016年，達美開始以737-900ER飛西雅圖—檀香山，其後又開航科納，但很快又改回757執飛：西岸至夏威夷之間沒有備降機場，延程飛行須攜帶足以中途折返的備用燃油，額外重量經常迫使飛機限載，影響收益。聯合航空以737-900ER飛夏威夷時也遇到同樣的問題，但其757機隊較小、且多為平躺商務艙配置，達美則有大量國內線配置的757可調度。如今達美夏威夷航線主要交給A321neo，聯合航空則用737 MAX；達美828架窄體客機中僅100多架具延程認證，約半數A321neo有認證——夠用就好，與聯合航空追求調度彈性的做法形成對比。

en.title: Why Delta keeps ETOPS certification on some Boeing 737-900ERs that never fly over oceans
en.summary: Delta's Boeing 737-900ERs fly only within North America, yet about 20 of them still hold ETOPS-180 certification — not for transoceanic flying, but for more efficient Caribbean routings and the Hawaii operation they once flew. Certification is expensive, so Delta has stripped it from most of the fleet, while United takes the opposite approach and certifies every 737 it flies.
body: Delta ordered 100 Boeing 737-900ERs in 2011, added 20 in 2015 and 10 more in 2017 for a total of 130, and acquired another 33 second-hand aircraft after COVID, with deliveries starting in 2013. The largest 737 variant has become a workhorse of Delta's domestic network, yet it is not known for exceptional range and flies only within North America. Even so, some of the fleet is certified for ETOPS-180 operations, meaning the aircraft may fly up to 180 minutes from a diversion airfield.

ETOPS stands for Extended-range Twin-engine Operational Performance Standards, and certification shows a twin-engine aircraft may safely fly more than 60 minutes from a diversion airfield, with the number denoting the permitted distance in minutes. It is an expensive capability: an aircraft needs additional communications and navigation equipment, maintenance under a special ETOPS programme, a pre-flight service check by an ETOPS-qualified mechanic, and its engines inspected by two separate technicians. Delta now maintains ETOPS certification on only about 20 of its 737-900ERs, having removed the extra equipment from many others. United, by contrast, certifies all 640 of its 737s and all 61 of its 757s, including 12 737-900s that mainly fly short domestic trips out of Houston.

Delta once planned a bigger role for the type. In 2016 it began flying the 737-900ER between Seattle and Honolulu, adding Kona shortly afterwards, but pulled the aircraft off the routes and put the 757 back on: with no diversion airports between the West Coast and Hawaii, an ETOPS flight must carry enough fuel to essentially turn around midway, and the extra weight frequently left the aircraft payload-restricted, hurting revenue. United faced the same problem flying the 737-900ER to Hawaii, but its 757 fleet was smaller and mostly configured with lie-flat business class seats, while Delta could fall back on its large subfleets of domestic-configured 757s. Today Delta mainly relies on the A321neo for Hawaii, while United uses the 737 MAX; just over 100 of Delta's 828 narrowbodies hold ETOPS certification, including about half of its A321neos — enough for what the airline needs, and a deliberate contrast with United's flexibility-first approach.
